related_questions.question: What is the obligation assessment in Texas?

text_blocks.snippet: In Texas, the Obligation Assessment (OA) is a component of the unemployment insurance tax rate for employers, used to cover bond obligations and interest payments on federal loans for unemployment benefits. The OA is composed of the Bond Obligation Assessment Rate and the Interest Tax Rate. For 2025, both the Obligation Assessment Ratio and Yield Margin are 0.00%, meaning there is no Obligation Assessment for Texas employers in 2025, according to the Texas Workforce Commission.
snippet_highlighted_words: a component of the unemployment insurance tax rate for employers, used to cover bond obligations and interest payments on federal loans for unemployment benefits

list.title: Purpose:
list.snippet: The OA is designed to ensure timely payment of interest on federal loans and to fulfill bond obligations related to the state's unemployment insurance program.

list.title: Components:
list.snippet: The OA consists of two parts: the Bond Obligation Assessment Rate and the Interest Tax Rate.

list.title: Calculation:
list.snippet: The Obligation Assessment Ratio (OA Ratio) is calculated based on outstanding bond obligations and taxes due, according to the Texas Workforce Commission. The Interest Tax Rate is calculated to cover interest payments on federal loans.

list.title: Deficit Tax Rate (DTR):
list.snippet: The DTR is a separate component of the tax rate, added when the unemployment insurance trust fund is below a minimum level. It is not part of the OA.

list.title: 2025 Rates:
list.snippet: The Obligation Assessment Ratio (OA Ratio) and Yield Margin are both 0.00% for 2025. There is no Interest Tax Rate assessed for 2025, and the Deficit Tax Rate is also 0.00%.

list.title: Total Rate:
list.snippet: The total unemployment tax rate for Texas employers in 2025 ranges from 0.25% to 6.25% and includes the General Tax Rate, Replenishment Tax Rate, OA, DTR, and Employment and Training Investment Assessment (ETIA).

related_questions.question: What is tax assessment vs property tax in Texas?
related_questions.snippet: Government tax assessors assign property owners a valuation every year as a means of measuring property taxes. The assessed value of a property is often lower than its appraised value or true market value. Tax-assessed values are used by your local government to determine how much property tax you should pay.

related_questions.question: What is TX SUI on my paycheck?

text_blocks.snippet: "TX SUI" on your paycheck refers to Texas State Unemployment Insurance, a state-level payroll tax that funds unemployment benefits for eligible workers. Employers primarily pay this tax, but some states may have provisions for employee contributions. The rate at which an employer pays SUI tax can vary based on factors like the employer's industry, experience, and the number of former employees who have claimed unemployment benefits.

list.title: What it is:
list.snippet: SUI is a state-specific tax that provides financial assistance to individuals who have lost their jobs through no fault of their own and meet the state's eligibility requirements.

list.title: Who pays:
list.snippet: In most states, including Texas, employers are primarily responsible for paying SUI taxes.

list.title: How it works:
list.snippet: The funds collected from SUI taxes are used to pay unemployment benefits to eligible workers.

list.title: Factors affecting rates:
list.snippet: SUI tax rates are often adjusted based on an employer's history of unemployment claims. Employers with more former employees claiming benefits may see their SUI tax rate increase.

list.title: Texas-specific information:
list.snippet: Texas has its own SUI tax rate schedule and wage base, which can be found on the Texas Workforce Commission website.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, the TX SUI tax on your paycheck is a contribution towards a state-level program that provides financial support to individuals who become unemployed.
